thread:
maria: FYI Northfield is seeing intermittent 429s and 2–3s tail latency on their dedicated pool. Customer says it started ~30m ago after a steady traffic increase. I can see a lot of scale up/down events in the last 25m. tagging @jonas @harper :eyes:

sre-bot: autoscaler/northfield-dedicated: desired=0 -> 2 (2026-03-16T14:02:11Z), desired=2 -> 0 (2026-03-16T14:05:03Z), desired=0 -> 2 (2026-03-16T14:07:58Z). cooldown=60s, policy=cpu_threshold.

jonas: Ugh, classic oscillation. Do we know which metric is tripping the scale? CPU, queue length, or GC pauses?

maria: Prom query shows rapid queue_length oscillations. snippets: 
```
avg_over_time(request_queue_length[1m]) spikes to 18 -> drops to 1 repeatedly
instance_cpu_utilization ~ 45-70% with short 10s bursts
```
Customer load pattern is bursty (chat app prefetches).

harper: Bursty client behavior + 60s cooldown is dangerously low for warmup. Nodes take ~90s to fully serve due to model weight loading/kv warmup. If desired goes to 0 while requests are still in-flight, we get 429s.

sam: Repro steps from my side: hitting the dedicated route with a 40rps ramp for 90s then drop to 1rps reproduces the churn. curl example: `for i in {1..400}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://dedicated.northfield.api/redwood/v1/generate; done` - I saw 429s when desired hit 0.

dylan: We should be careful: scale-to-zero is enabled for this pool to save cost. For latency-sensitive customers we recommend min_replicas=1 or prewarm. Suggest temporary mitigation: set min_replicas=2 and bump cooldown to 300s while we investigate.

jonas: Agreed. Also add a stabilization window for the CPU metric: require 3/5 samples above threshold before scaling up and similar for down. That prevents reacting to 10s spikes.

maria: I'll run the short patch now: `infractl autoscale update --pool northfield-dedicated --min-replicas 2 --cooldown 300 --stabilization 300s` — applying in staging then prod in 5m.

sre-bot: change-request: infractl applied to northfield-dedicated by maria at 2026-03-16T14:12:34Z. new config: min_replicas=2, cooldown=300s, stabilization=300s.

harper: After the change, watch for cost alerts. Also file a follow-up to evaluate prewarming (keep a small warm pool during off-peak) and document a recommended autopolicy for dedicated customers with heavy tail latency.

sam: I notified Northfield support contact and asked for a validation window. They said they'll run their load tests and report back.

maria: Quick post-change metrics: no scale-to-zero events in the last 10m, queue_length max=3, p95 latency dropped from 3.2s -> 450ms. Customer just confirmed they no longer see 429s. :thumbsup:

dylan: Nice. Next steps: (1) add an autoscale policy template for latency-sensitive dedicated pools, (2) add observability dashboard showing warmup progress (kv cache fill, model loaded flag), (3) run a cost/benefit for min_replicas vs burst credits. I'll open tickets.

jonas: Also add a unit in the incident playbook to check `scale-to-zero`/`min_replicas` for customer reports of transient 429s. Had this come up before and we didn't catch the zeroing.

maria: Filed RN-4572 (runbook update) and INF-2291 (autoscale policy template). Closing this thread once tickets are linked to the customer case.

sre-bot: ticket RN-4572 created by maria. ticket INF-2291 created by dylan.

sam: Customer follow-up scheduled for 2026-03-16T15:00Z.

maria: Marking as resolved for now. Will reopen if flapping resumes. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
